terms.comment: Between too much and too little (Cic. Off. 1.89, Lewis & Short). Of people and their gifts it can mean ordinary, mediocre (ōrātōrēs mediocrēs, Cic. Brut. 136); nōn mediocris is remarkable.
Keeping to a measure; of size, moderate. It can also mean small, scanty (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: moderate, of a person: restrained, temperate

phrases.latin: Mediocrī spatiō relictō Pullō pīlum in hostēs immittit
phrases.english: Leaving a moderate distance, Pullo hurls his javelin at the enemy

phrases.latin: intrā hās mediocrī lātitūdine fossam tēctīs mīlitibus obdūcī jussit
phrases.english: behind these he had a trench of medium width dug, with the soldiers under cover

mediocris.against: Lewis & Short mediō̆cris, “ō usually; rarely ŏ”
mediocris.html: De Vaan 424, s.v. ocris, prints mediocris without a macron and derives it from ocris, “rugged mountain” (PIE *h₂ok-r-i-): “orig. ‘situated at the middle, half-way of the top’”. In verse the vowel stands before cr, so the syllable can be heavy by position and the metre cannot show a long vowel (Hor. AP 370, 372).
